name: TLV1117-33CDCYR
title: TLV1117: 15 V, 800 mA linear regulator, fixed and adjustable
summary: The TLV1117 is a positive linear regulator for loads up to 800 mA from 2.7 V to 15 V in, with fixed outputs of 1.5, 1.8, 2.5, 3.3 and 5 V and an adjustable version (1.25 V reference, 1.25 V to 13.8 V out). It ships as a legacy chip or a new chip; the new-chip fixed version draws 65 µA typical quiescent current and adds soft-start, foldback current limit, UVLO, thermal shutdown and an output pull-down, and needs no minimum load. Packages are SOT-223, TO-252, TO-263, TO-220 and WSON-8. TLV1117-33CDCYR is the 3.3 V, 0 °C to 125 °C version in SOT-223 on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Simplified application, adjustable regulator
circuits.description: The adjustable TLV1117 between 100 µF input and output capacitors. R1 runs from VOUT to ADJ and carries the current I1 set by VREF across it; the variable R2 from ADJ to ground sets the output. IADJ leaves the ADJ pin into the same node.

circuits.title: Best load regulation using the adjustable regulator
circuits.description: R1 is taken straight from the OUTPUT pin, ahead of the line resistance Rt1 to the load, and the bottom of R2 goes to the ground end of the load, ahead of the return resistance Rt2. VLOAD = VREF × (R1 + R2) / R1 – IL × Rt1.

circuits.title: Regulator with protection diode
circuits.description: Adjustable regulator with R1 from VOUT to ADJ, R2 from ADJ to ground, a 10 µF capacitor from ADJ to ground and 100 µF on the output. The optional 1N4002 has its anode on VOUT and cathode on VIN, so a large output capacitor discharges through it when the input is shorted.

circuits.title: Reverse current protection with a Schottky diode
circuits.description: A fixed new-chip regulator with CIN and COUT; a Schottky diode from OUT (anode) to IN (cathode) parallels the internal body diode and carries reverse current around the part.

circuits.title: Basic adjustable regulator
circuits.description: The adjustable version with 10 µF on the input, 100 µF on the output, R1 from OUTPUT to ADJ/GND and the variable R2 from ADJ/GND to ground, so VOUT = VREF × (1 + R2/R1) + IADJ × R2. CADJ from ADJ/GND to ground raises ripple rejection; the 1N4002 from output (anode) to input (cathode) protects the part if the input is suddenly shorted.

operation.text: Any TLV1117 order code may arrive built on the legacy die or on the new die; the fab source code on the packaging label tells them apart (CSO: RFB or FFAB is the new chip, CSO: SFB the legacy chip). New-chip packages: DCY (SOT-223), KVU and NDP (TO-252). Legacy-chip packages: DRJ (WSON), KCS and KCT (TO-220), KTT (TO-263). Legacy-chip thermal figures exist for DCY, KVU and the KTE and KTP PowerFlex packages as well.

A positive linear regulator for up to 800 mA, with fixed outputs from 1.5 V to 5 V and an adjustable output from 1.25 V to 13.8 V, from 2.7 V to 15 V in. The adjustable part holds 1.25 V (VREF) between OUTPUT and ADJ. The new-chip circuitry runs down to 1.5 V across the part, and dropout is 1.3 V maximum at 800 mA, less at lower current. The new-chip fixed version adds foldback current limit, thermal shutdown, an internal output pull-down and UVLO; inside, it regulates through an internal divider against a 0.8 V bandgap reference.

The adjustable version needs a load of at least 1.7 mA typical (5 mA maximum over the electrical table) to regulate, and wants at least 10 µF of tantalum on its output for stability and transient response. The new-chip fixed version has no minimum load. On the legacy chip the bias current flows out of the OUT pin, so the load or the feedback divider must take at least the minimum load current or the output can rise.
An internal soft-start limits inrush current at turn-on, which lets the input capacitor be smaller.

Dropout is VIN – VOUT at the rated current with the pass transistor fully on; it sets the least input above the nominal output that keeps regulation. The pass device is a CMOS transistor, so dropout is its on-resistance times the current and shrinks at lighter load. Below VOUT(nom) + VDO the part is in dropout: the output follows the input and transient response is much worse. On leaving dropout the output can overshoot briefly while the pass transistor is pulled back out of full drive.

operation.topic: Foldback current limit (fixed output, new chip)
operation.text: The limit is a hybrid: above VFOLDBACK = 50% of VOUT(nom) it is brick-wall at ICL, and below that it folds back as the output falls toward ground, to ISC with the output shorted. The output is not regulated while limiting. The part heats at (VIN – VOUT) × ICL or (VIN – VOUT) × ISC; if thermal shutdown trips, the part turns off and restarts when cool, and a lasting fault makes it cycle between current limit and thermal shutdown.

A separate UVLO circuit watches the input and turns the output on and off cleanly. Its hysteresis (130 mV typical) keeps a dip in the input during turn-on from turning the part off. With VIN at 1.8 V, below the falling threshold, the regulator is off, and with 2.5 V applied to VOUT the output pull-down sinks 0.7 mA to 1.1 mA.

The part turns off when the pass-transistor junction reaches TSD(shutdown), 180 °C typical, and back on below TSD(reset), 160 °C typical. The die's thermal time constant is short, so the part cycles on and off until dissipation drops. Start-up with a large VIN – VOUT or a large output capacitor can trip it before the output is up. Continuous running into shutdown or above the recommended junction temperature shortens life; the protection does not replace heat sinking.

The part regulates the voltage between OUTPUT and ADJ, so wiring resistance between regulator and load adds error. Take R1 from the OUTPUT pin rather than from the load, and return the bottom of R2 to the load's ground for remote ground sensing. With 0.05 Ω between a 5 V regulator and its load, the error is 0.05 Ω × IL with R1 at the regulator, but 0.05 Ω × (1 + R2/R1) × IL — four times larger with R1 = 125 Ω — if R1 is tied at the load.

In normal use no protection diodes are needed. Internal resistance between ADJ and OUTPUT limits current even with a capacitor on ADJ, and ADJ survives ±25 V transients relative to the output. The internal output-to-input diode takes microsecond surges of 10 A to 20 A when the input is shorted and the output capacitor discharges back. With 1000 µF or more on the output and an input shorted instantly, the part can be damaged; then fit an external diode from output (anode) to input (cathode).

Stable with low-ESR ceramic capacitors on input and output; X7R, X5R and C0G dielectrics hold their value well over temperature, Y5V is not advised. Expect effective capacitance to fall by up to 50% with voltage and temperature. An input capacitor is not needed for stability but helps transient response, ripple and PSRR; use one when the source impedance is above 0.5 Ω, and a larger one for fast large transients or a source several inches away. Output ESR must be 2 mΩ to 500 mΩ; with a higher-ESR capacitor, add a low-ESR ceramic. A bigger output capacitor reduces overshoot and undershoot.

The output capacitor sets stability: the part is stable with tantalum or aluminium electrolytic output capacitors of 0.2 Ω to 10 Ω ESR, and larger values improve transient response and loop stability. CADJ from ADJ to ground raises ripple rejection; when it is fitted, COUT must be larger than CADJ. Fit CIN when the regulator is not near the supply's filter capacitor.

TLV1117-3.3 from a 12 V input: keep VIN – VOUT above the 3.3 V version's dropout over load and temperature, use 1.0 µF on the output for good load-transient response, and an optional input capacitor to lower source impedance and improve transient response.

Reverse current flows through the pass transistor's body diode, is not limited inside, and degrades reliability when large. It arises when a large COUT is left charged as the input collapses at light load, when the output is driven before the input is up, or when the output is held above the input; each can break the VOUT ≤ VIN + 0.3 V rating. Where it is expected, add external protection such as a Schottky diode from output to input.

Keep other hot parts away from the regulator and size the copper for the dissipation. On packages with a thermal pad, the pad is the main heat path: solder it to a copper area with an array of plated vias to inner or bottom planes. RθJA depends heavily on copper area, weight and plane position; the table values use the JEDEC standard board and are for comparing packages. The ψJT and ψJB parameters barely depend on copper area and give TJ from a measured package-top or board temperature. Pick the lowest input voltage that still regulates to keep dissipation down.

Fixed and adjustable versions have different recommended input ranges. Fit one or two input capacitors if the regulator is not close to the supply's output filter capacitor, to filter high-frequency noise and brief surges, and make the input and output traces wide enough for the full current to keep I×R drop small.
Suited to post-regulating a DC/DC converter output, to battery chargers and to processor supply rails; on the adjustable version a capacitor on ADJ gives very high ripple rejection.
